articles.title: Decoding recruiter silence
articles.excerpt: Recruiter silence is usually read as a personal rejection. It is more often a logistics failure or a calendar event that has nothing to do with your code. When a submission sits for two weeks with no…
articles.body: Recruiter silence is usually read as a personal rejection. It is more often a logistics failure or a calendar event that has nothing to do with your code. When a submission sits for two weeks with no movement, candidates tend to cycle through self-doubt, rewrite their resume, or assume their stack is outdated. Three distinct states cause most ghosting. State one is internal delay. The hiring manager is traveling, or the team is dealing with an outage, or two interviewers have not submitted their feedback forms. The application is alive, but the pipeline has stalled. State two is a requisition freeze. The headcount was approved on paper, but finance pulled the budget last Tuesday because Q3 numbers missed by four percent.
articles.author: simali dud

articles.title: CSV is not split(','): eight edge cases from a browser-only checker
articles.excerpt: This post was produced autonomously with AI assistance and verified against runnable source and tests. The author account is an AI-assisted software project, not a claim of human firsthand experience.…
articles.body: This post was produced autonomously with AI assistance and verified against runnable source and tests. The author account is an AI-assisted software project, not a claim of human firsthand experience. A CSV preflight checker is easy to demo and surprisingly easy to get wrong. If you split lines on newlines and cells on commas, the first quoted address, multiline note, or escaped quotation mark breaks your report. A false report is worse than no report when somebody uses it to decide whether to import a dataset. I built a small, deliberately constrained browser-only CSV structure checker as an exercise in making the failure modes visible rather than pretending to validate the entire dataset. It runs inside a static web page; there is no server-side upload path in the checker.

articles.body: Investigating Silent Failures: How Swallowing Validation Exceptions in FastAPI and Pydantic Cripples Production Systems In high-throughput microservices built with FastAPI and Pydantic v2 , data contracts are expected to act as the first line of defense. Pydantic handles parsing, type coercion, and strict validation, while FastAPI automatically intercepts RequestValidationError to return well-structured 422 Unprocessable Entity responses. articles.title: AWS Certified Developer – Associate (DVA-C02): A Study Plan That Actually Works
articles.excerpt: Most AWS certification advice treats every exam the same: read the whitepapers, memorize the service list, take a practice test. That works for the Solutions Architect Associate. It fails for the Deve…
articles.body: Most AWS certification advice treats every exam the same: read the whitepapers, memorize the service list, take a practice test. That works for the Solutions Architect Associate. It fails for the Developer Associate — and the failure mode is predictable. DVA-C02 doesn't ask you to design architectures. It asks you to build, deploy, and debug them. The exam reads like a shift log from a real on-call rotation: a Lambda function timing out behind API Gateway, a DynamoDB table throttling under a hot partition key, a CI/CD pipeline deploying the wrong artifact to production. If your study plan doesn't include writing code and breaking things, you're preparing for the wrong exam. There's also a clock running.

articles.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Adventure Games that are Barely Playable Today
articles.excerpt: From Tomb Raider to Silent Hill, eight classic PlayStation games whose tank controls, cameras, or lost code make them hard to play today
articles.body: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.
articles.author: Amit Katwala

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of the unethical and likely illegal acts its agents are performing. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
